# Packaging and release (area `release`)

Building and signing FERB.app and DMGs, versions, appcasts, release checks, the logo assets and the public site.

Active decisions here. Run `tools/kb/run kb show <file>` for the ones governing one file, their tests and open work; never reword an owner decision (supersede it).

- **REL-1** (owner): FERB's one logo is the extension's: the dark rounded square with the white "f" and the orange dot, unchanged in look, used by the app, the site, the extension and everywhere else.
- **REL-2** (owner): A release refuses a version that is a .dev one, not newer than the last v* tag on origin, or not the tag's, and one whose extension the Chrome Web Store doesn't serve yet (MIN_EXTENSION_VERSION). Tests keep ferb/__init__.py and pyproject.toml equal and the repo's extension at or above MIN_EXTENSION_VERSION. The version stays 0.27.0.dev1 for now.
- **REL-4** (agent): FERB.app and its helper name CFBundleIconFile AppIcon; build-app.sh copies the icns into their Resources and build-dmg.sh sets it as the disk image's volume icon. No Icon Composer .icon compiled by actool into Assets.car.
- **REL-404** (agent): FERB.app never compiles ferb-secrets: build-app.sh ships the arm64 or x86_64 slice of assets/secret-helper/ferb-secrets after scripts/secret_helper.py --check confirms pin.json matches the binary and the helper's code (comments aside). Only a change to the helper's code is rebuilt and pinned again (--build), knowing every saved secret then asks once more on each Mac.
- **REL-408** (owner): The disk image opens as a designed Finder window: fixed size, no toolbar or sidebar, large icons, FERB left and the Applications link right with an arrow between, over a still of FERB's startup field (Gravity — Dense) with words in the system font; no text file. Before the Developer ID it says "Drag FERB to Applications" and that macOS blocks FERB the first time (System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway); after it (Developer ID, notarized: the variant that stays) only the drag line. The signing identity picks the variant.
- **REL-409** (owner): The whole window (heading, both icons with their names, the first-open note) is visible at once with margins, Finder never scrolls it, and it fits a 1440 x 900 screen with the menu bar and the Dock. The names FERB and Applications read in white on the field.
- **REL-411** (agent): Finder draws icon labels black over a background picture in any appearance; no view option changes it (macOS 27.2: icvp textColor in any form is ignored). So the background draws the names in white, and Finder's labels, at its smallest size (10), fall on a soft pool of the stage's black under each icon, unseen. Labels to the right scroll the window sideways. WindowBounds is the whole window: the 680 x 440 content plus a 32-point title bar (macOS 26+); on a 28-point title bar the window is 4 points taller than the picture (macOS 15 not checked).
- **REL-412** (owner): ferb.kartikey.xyz is one calm page in the manner of kartikey.xyz (narrow column, system type, thin rules, quiet links), with words from the earlier site; no glass, gradients or notch walkthrough demo. Still held: REL-1's logo and its derived files; only the Apple Silicon DMG with an Apple icon, inactive until the owner gives its URL; the first-open note; /privacy at the same URL; privacy claims keep local storage and redacted context to the chosen AI service, never all-offline AI; PostHog last (REL-407).
- **REL-415** (owner): The version is 0.27.0 (ferb/__init__.py, pyproject.toml, uv.lock), tagged v0.27.0 and published as a GitHub release carrying the Apple Silicon DMG and its Sparkle appcast. Replaces REL-2's "The version stays 0.27.0.dev1 for now"; the rest of REL-2 (no .dev release, newer than the last tag, the store serves the extension minimum) holds.
- **REL-418** (owner): The version is 0.27.3 (ferb/__init__.py, pyproject.toml, uv.lock), tagged v0.27.3 and published as the GitHub release whose appcast offers the update to installed copies, after the owner's local test. REL-415's 0.27.0 stays the first release.
- **REL-419** (owner): scripts/developer-team.txt holds FERB's Apple Developer ID Team ID, 8N7RNGH974: public and tracked, the counterpart of scripts/release-cert.sha1.
- **REL-420** (owner): One FERB.app shipped as two DMGs (Apple silicon, Intel), the app and each DMG signed with FERB's Apple Developer ID and notarized; updates install by themselves; the notch is the main interface with detail in a regular window; installing from source stays supported. Replaces REL-403's "signed without a Developer ID or notarization for now"; the rest of REL-403 holds.
- **REL-421** (agent): SIGN_IDENTITY=devid signs with the one valid "Developer ID Application" identity of scripts/developer-team.txt's team, by its SHA-1 (none or two refuse; its name is never printed). Pieces keep codesign's default requirement and are verified against identifier + anchor apple generic + leaf OU = team; library validation stays on; app and DMG are notarized and stapled. A DMG takes only a stapled, Gatekeeper-notarized team app and is itself checked with spctl; release-appcast.sh refuses any other DMG before EdDSA signing. Release mode stays until the first devid release passes its live checks.
- **REL-422** (agent): signing.sh picks the code it signs by file(1)'s Mach-O type, not by name or execute bit, and after signing verifies every Mach-O file in the bundle with codesign --verify --strict, in every mode; in devid mode each must also meet the team requirement unless it is another team's Developer ID code kept as its vendor signed it (Codex, Claude Code). One failure stops the build before notarization and names the file.
- **REL-423** (agent): For APP-903. release-appcast.sh reads the DMG app's TeamIdentifier; the first team-signed release writes its build (the earlier of the two architectures') to scripts/developer-id-first-build.txt, to be committed, and make_appcast.py puts it in every later item as sparkle:minimumAutoupdateVersion. A minimum above the build being published is refused.
- **REL-424** (agent): FERB_NOTARIZE=0 with SIGN_IDENTITY=devid signs every piece with the team's Developer ID exactly as REL-421 (timestamp, team requirement, library validation) and skips notarization and stapling, needing no notary credentials. build-dmg.sh refuses FERB_NOTARIZE=0, and ferb_check_devid_app (a DMG's app, release-appcast.sh) still requires a stapled, Gatekeeper-notarized app, so such a build is never shipped.
- **REL-425** (agent): FERB's version is rust/crates/ferbd/src/compose/mod.rs VERSION, and rust/Cargo.toml's [workspace.package] version is the same; a release-tooling test checks both. build-app-rust.sh (rust-parts.sh ferb_rust_pins), `ferb --version`, the store's build record and release_checks.py's messages use it. These are REL-2's two files that must agree; ferb/__init__.py and pyproject.toml no longer hold it.
- **REL-426** (agent): scripts/sign-app.sh APP is the one re-signing path (was build-app.sh --sign-only): signing.sh's ferb_sign_app then ferb_notarize_built, under SIGN_IDENTITY and FERB_NOTARIZE as a build signs; no rebuild. build-dmg.sh with no app builds each with build-app-rust.sh. release-appcast.sh refuses a DMG whose app carries Contents/Resources/python and reads the extension pins from the Rust sources only. - **REL-427** (agent): scripts/dmg_layout.py is the one spec. make_dmg_background.py (stdlib) compiles dmg-background/main.swift with the app's StartupStudies.swift and GravityDenseStudy.swift and renders each variant at 1x and 2x into assets/dmg, committed (REL-428). build-dmg.sh stages FERB.app, the Applications link, a 1x+2x TIFF background and the volume icon, then dmg_layout.py writes the .DS_Store on the mounted image with ds_store and mac_alias (MIT; pinned by its PEP 723 metadata and scripts/dmg_layout.py.lock, `uv run --script --locked`), never driving Finder; alias and bookmark name /Volumes/FERB.
- **REL-428** (agent): assets/logo/ferb-logo.svg is the one master (128-unit canvas, the 96-unit square inset 16; the "f" an outline path, so nothing depends on installed fonts). Change the logo only there, then run `uv run --script --locked scripts/make_logo.py` (PyObjC pinned in its PEP 723 metadata and scripts/make_logo.py.lock), which rewrites every derived file (PNG, AppIcon.icns, extension and notch SVGs and PNGs, site favicon and touch icon) with macOS's own renderer and iconutil. Derived files are committed, so builds don't render.
- **REL-429** (owner): No build refuses FERB.app for its size. build-app-rust.sh prints the size report (ferb_rust_size_report) so growth stays visible.
- **REL-430** (owner): A public GitHub repo, Json604/ferb-update, holds only releases (DMGs and appcasts), no source; the source repo stays private (PROJ-513). Built by the coordinator 2026-11-17 (REL-432): the site's redirects send FERB's update and download paths there.
- **REL-431** (owner): From now on every address a shipped FERB build uses for FERB's own services can move without touching installed copies or any manual step. The copies installed today (his and a friend's) are updated by hand once; no bridge release in the old repo.
- **REL-432** (agent): For REL-431. Every address a shipped build contacts for FERB's own services is under the owner's domain (ferb.kartikey.xyz), never a host's name; the site redirects it (307) to where the thing lives (ferb-update's releases now): the feed (/updates/appcast-ARCH.xml), the appcast's files and notes, the download. A build carries an ordered list of feeds (UpdatePlan.feedPrefixes: the owner's domain first, then the releases' own address), asks the next only when one can't be had, never any other; only an update FERB's EdDSA key signed installs.
- **REL-435** (owner): ferb.kartikey.xyz runs PostHog with session recordings and every analytics part that is needed or helpful, not a minimal setup.
- **REL-438** (owner): For REL-435. Every visit to the website is counted, anonymously, as Google Analytics' consent mode does: also before the visitor answers, after No thanks, and with Do Not Track or Global Privacy Control. The full analytics and recordings still wait for OK.
- **REL-439** (agent): For REL-435, REL-438. With POSTHOG_KEY/HOST set the static pages load /analytics.js and the pinned, bundled, hash-checked posthog-js. Until OK (and after No, and with DNT or GPC: no bar then) PostHog runs cookieless (on_reject, opt_out_capturing_by_default): nothing stored, no person, no recording; before_send passes only $pageview, $pageleave and download clicked (the site's download button, REL-442). OK opts in: everything REL-435 asks, inputs masked, no request bodies or headers. No after OK opts out and clears PostHog's storage. Only the toolbar may come from its servers.
- **REL-445** (owner): A FERB account sign-in (Google or Apple, REL-440) on a Mac or phone lasts 180 days from its last use: each rotating refresh token is valid 180 days from its issue, so an app left unused 180 days asks to sign in again. The 1-hour access token and REL-441's other limits (Send me the link, rate limits) are as REL-441 has them; his answer named only the lifetime.
- **REL-446** (owner): FERB pins no cryptography release for Intel Macs: no Python ships with FERB (ENG-2), so REL-402 has nothing to pin.
- **REL-447** (owner): Every FERB build sends Send to developer's reports to the relay at an address under the owner's domain (ferb.kartikey.xyz), so shipped copies never depend on a workers.dev address and the relay can move without touching installed copies (REL-431).
- **REL-448** (agent): For REL-447, as REL-432. site/vercel.json rewrites only /reports/file and /reports/report to the Worker (ferb-reports.ferb-reports.workers.dev), never a redirect. reports::RELAY_URLS, in order: ferb.kartikey.xyz/reports, then the Worker's own address, never another; [feedback] relay_url replaces both. Each step of a Send starts at the address that took the last one and moves on when it isn't taken (no answer or any refusal). The relay counts a request against its connecting address, then the X-Real-IP Vercel forwards, one key per address.
- **REL-449** (owner): FERB sends no email: no Send me the link, no update emails, no Resend, no unsubscribe link; no app or page says it may email you. The account is kept to know who uses FERB and to sign in on every device. Otherwise REL-440 and REL-442 stand: the three apps need a FERB account (Google or Apple only) before use, kept in the site's ferb_users (deleting it in an app deletes its row, devices and sign-ins); the site's Download is a plain link (/download/FILE, 307 to the latest release, REL-432), nothing asked; sign-in is in the app; the download sign-in's rows stay.
- **REL-450** (agent): For REL-449. Pages: static HTML, one stylesheet, light, no web fonts; no script but REL-439's analytics; server pages none (CSP default-src 'none'). Server: Vercel Functions in site/api (Node, ESM), shared code in site/api/_lib. Google sign-in: openid-client (code flow, PKCE, state, nonce). HMAC-SHA256 tokens with AUTH_SECRET naming their purpose: sign-in cookie 10 min, download link 10 min, admin cookie 8 h. List: Neon Postgres ferb_users (email, name, first sign-in, last download), made on first use; the admin page shows it and a CSV. No mail code, no unsubscribe endpoint.
- **REL-452** (agent): For REL-449, APP-1137. As REL-451 (start, callback, token, me, signout, delete, assertion, ready; PKCE codes; opaque rotating tokens, REL-445; rate limits) with: a Mac returns only to http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback (port 1024-65535, no leading zeros, nothing else in it), never ferb-auth://callback; apple: the iPhone's identity token checked against Apple's JWKS, audience com.ferb.phone, nonce = SHA-256 hex of the raw nonce sent, each nonce once in 10 minutes, then the code grant's account linking, device record, rate limit and answer.
- **REL-453** (owner): A sign-in the site ends (reused after a 60 s grace in which the old refresh token gets the same new pair; expired after 180 days; signed out) only asks to sign in again, with why: phones stay paired, the Mac keeps its phones; only a deleted account also unpairs a phone. A name never blocks sign-in. Each failure has its own true words. Delete succeeds only when the site confirms. The sign-in screens say to use the same account on both; Hide My Email is named in a mismatch. Sign-outs reach other devices on focus or open.
- **REL-454** (agent): For REL-453, refining REL-452's reuse. A rotation's pair is HMAC(AUTH_SECRET, old refresh token), issued at the rotation's time; the old token within 60 s, before the new one is used, gets it again. invalid_grant carries reason signed_out, expired or account_deleted (hashes in ferb_app_deleted). Sweep on every grant, bounded. Names: 200 code points, cut. A Mac start's errors 303 to its loopback. Android's landing uses an intent link. Schema runs unless ferb_app_limits carries the version comment. Owner list: providers, last sign-in, devices.
